evidence: The graphite susceptor is heated by an RF coil and the temperature is measured by a thermocouple imbedded in the graphite susceptor. The rotating susceptor allows controlled exposures to the precursors by rotation under windows in a stationary top plate. The substrates were semi-insulating (001) 2 ° toward [110] GaAs. Growth proceeded in cycles where one cycle consisted of a single rotation under the AsH3 window and the TMGa window.
